flawed_step: The essential step, 'every non-optimal tour T has a strictly shorter tour obtainable by replacing at most ceil(n/2) edges', cannot be justified. The only cheaper tour can differ from T in more than ceil(n/2) edges while every tour in between is more expensive.
counterexample:
n=12, k=6=ceil(12/2), cities 0..11 (indices mod 12), i=0..3. Weights: w(3i,3i+1)=0, w(3i+1,3i+2)=0, w(3i+2,3i+3)=5, w(3i,3i+2)=1, w(3i,3i+4)=2; every other edge weight 50. Call the 20 edges with weight <50 the graph G.
T = 0-1-2-...-11-0 has cost 4*(0+0+5)=20.
T* = 1-2-0-4-5-3-7-8-6-10-11-9-1 has cost 4*(0+1+2)=12. It shares only the 4 edges (3i+1,3i+2) with T, so it needs 8 > 6 replaced edges.
Claim: every tour other than T* costs at least 20.
- A tour using a weight-50 edge costs at least 50.
- Tours inside G: blocks B_i={3i,3i+1,3i+2}. Consecutive blocks are joined only by (3i+2,3i+3) and (3i,3i+4); non-consecutive blocks are not joined. Let c_i be the number of tour edges between B_i and B_{i+1}. Cutting at two boundaries gives c_i+c_j in {2,4}, so there are three cases.
  (a) All c_i=1: each block is a path. Entry by (3i-1,3i) is at 3i, and exit by (3i,3i+4) is also at 3i, so a weight-5 boundary edge cannot be followed by a weight-2 one. All boundaries have the same type, giving only T or T*.
  (b) All c_i=2: the forced edges form two 6-cycles (0-4-5-6-10-11-0 and its shift), so no tour.
  (c) One c_i=0, rest 2: the edges are forced, e.g. 0-1-2-3-7-8-9-11-10-6-5-4-0, cost 0+0+5+2+0+5+1+0+2+5+0+2=22 >= 20; rotations are the same.
So every tour within 6 replaced edges of T costs at least 20: T is a 6-opt local optimum, but T* costs 12 < 20, so T is not globally optimal.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. The instance has n=12, k=6, and blocks of 3 cities in which T and T* share one of three tour edges, so they differ in 8 edges, which is more than 6. The two edges joining consecutive blocks force all blocks to switch together. A cut-parity case analysis finds exactly T, T*, and 4 rotated tours of cost 22 inside the weight-<50 graph; every other tour costs at least 50. T (cost 20) is therefore 6-opt (and 7-opt) locally optimal but not optimal (T* costs 12).
